public_payload.normalized_proposition: There never has been and never will be an economically feasible way to offer LLM services without charging each user's actual token burn.

statement.excerpt: There has never been — and never will be — an economically-feasible way to offer services powered by LLMs without charging the actual token burn of each user, and in the process of deceiving said users, these companies have created products with illusory benefits and questionable return on investment.

from_speaker: without charging the actual token burn of each user
our_interpretation: This is an unconditional, unlimited-horizon impossibility claim, including a historical assertion.
The ordinary reading is that sustainable LLM services must bill actual individual token consumption.
Flat fees, seat pricing or fixed task prices can qualify as counterexamples even if the provider internally measures tokens.
The normalized proposition concerns pricing feasibility. The additional allegations about deception, benefits and return on investment are not separately adjudicated here.
No particular company's monetary metric is asserted, so metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: An empirical search cannot establish impossibility for all future services. Support would require a general economic constraint proving that every qualifying alternative must fail.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented LLM service sustains positive service-level economics while charging on a basis other than each user's actual token consumption.
